slot.brief: Evaluate statements on maximum/minimum oxidation states across the 3d series (why Mn max is +7, why Cu +2 vs +1 stability) — moderate reasoning, pick the true set.

stem: Consider the following statements about oxidation states in the $3d$ series. (I) The highest commonly attained oxidation state rises from Sc ($+3$) to Mn ($+7$), then generally falls toward Zn. (II) Mn reaches $+7$ because all seven valence electrons in $3d^5 4s^2$ can participate in bonding. (III) In aqueous solution, Cu$^{+}$ is more stable than Cu$^{2+}$ because Cu$^{+}$ has a $d^{10}$ configuration. (IV) Aqueous Cu$^{+}$ tends to disproportionate to Cu$^{2+}$ and Cu. Which set contains all and only the correct statements?

verdicts.working: I is true: the maximum commonly attained oxidation state rises to Mn and then generally falls. II is true: Mn can use its seven 3d and 4s valence electrons. III is false; aqueous Cu⁺ is unstable relative to Cu²⁺ and Cu. IV is true: Cu⁺ disproportionates. Thus only I, II and IV are correct.

working:
I: Sc $+3$ to Mn $+7$, then generally lower; II: Mn $3d^5 4s^2$ has 7 valence electrons. Both true. III: false; $d^{10}$ alone does not favour aqueous Cu$^{+}$. IV: $2\text{Cu}^{+}(aq)\rightarrow\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)+\text{Cu}(s)$. Correct set: A.

Independent check: I is true: the maximum commonly attained oxidation state rises to Mn and then generally falls. II is true: Mn can use its seven 3d and 4s valence electrons. III is false; aqueous Cu⁺ is unstable relative to Cu²⁺ and Cu. IV is true: Cu⁺ disproportionates. Thus only I, II and IV are correct.
solution:
The maximum commonly attained oxidation state rises from Sc to Mn and then generally falls; Mn can use its seven valence electrons, $3d^5 4s^2$ (I, II true). In aqueous solution, Cu$^+$ disproportionates despite its $d^{10}$ configuration:
$$2\text{Cu}^{+}(aq)\rightarrow\text{Cu}^{2+}(aq)+\text{Cu}(s)$$
Thus III is false, while IV is true; the correct set is I, II and IV.
